summary: Navdeep Bains is the new Ontario Liberal leader, S&P warns it may cut Ontario's credit rating, and Canada's defence minister says he sees no change in military ties despite a reported Pentagon memo.
body: Ontario Liberals chose Navdeep Bains as their leader on Saturday. The party says he won on the third ballot with 50.29 per cent of the vote, out of about 20,500 votes cast.[^2] Bains was a federal Liberal MP from Mississauga for 13 years and Canada's industry minister, then worked as a bank and telecom executive. He does not have a seat in the provincial legislature, and he replaces Bonnie Crombie, who stepped down earlier this year.[^1] He says he wants to bring well-paying jobs to Ontario and will take on Premier Doug Ford's government.[^2]

Ontario's finances got a warning. Credit rating agency S&P Global put the province on a "negative outlook", meaning it sees at least a one-in-three chance of lowering Ontario's AA rating within two years. A lower rating can make borrowing more expensive. Ontario now expects a $16.9 billion deficit this year, and interest on its debt costs $17.3 billion a year. Finance Minister Peter Bethlenfalvy says he is confident Ontario will keep its rating and blames US tariffs and high interest rates; he says he will look for savings without raising taxes.[^3]

At the Halifax International Security Forum on Saturday, Defence Minister David McGuinty said he had not seen a classified memo from US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth that, according to the Washington Post, limits US defence co-operation with Canada. He said military co-operation is "business as usual".[^4] A Pentagon spokesperson said engagement with Canada must advance US defence goals, but that intelligence sharing, NORAD and NATO work are not affected. McGuinty also said Canada will put an initial $100 million into the NATO Innovation Fund, which invests in new defence technology.[^5]
Otherwise it was a quiet weekend, with no public update on the Stellantis Brampton plant talks.
differences: On Ontario's finances, Bethlenfalvy calls the S&P warning routine and "not a hinge moment", while Liberal MPP Stephanie Bowman says the government is in a "downward spiral" and a downgrade would cost taxpayers more.[^3] On the memo, the Pentagon says ties with Canada must serve US goals, while McGuinty says he has seen no change so far.[^4][^5]
